<description>
While playing around with pruning for the kernel, I noticed that only bitcoind's init locks the blocks directory (`AppInitLockDirectories`). The kernel doesn't.

Pointing a kernel program at a running node's data directory fails, but only because LevelDB locks `blocks/index`. To avoid a second copy of the chain, the obvious workaround is to use the node's blocks directory with the program's own data directory, or in-memory databases. It starts without error, but with an empty block index `BlockManager` writes from offset 0 of the node's `blk00000.dat`, which `FlatFileSeq::Open` opens in place with `"rb+"`. The node keeps running and serves the overwritten bytes as its own blocks.

#31674 added the blocks directory lock to bitcoind and noted that "the kernel does not currently do any dir locking, but it should". This PR follows sedited's [suggestion](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/31674#pullrequestreview-2560427054) to add the lock to the `BlockManager` constructor, and is based on the [`lock_blocksdir_raii`](https://github.com/sedited/bitcoin/commit/e08ecc19b37b23ee936c3b14b75b3852efd1d23c) commit.

`BlockManager` holds `.lock` for its whole lifetime through `BlocksDirLock`, its first member, so the directory is locked before `xor.dat` is touched. Creating a chainstate manager on a blocks directory locked by another process, bitcoind or a kernel user, fails.

In bitcoind, init already holds the lock, so `LockDirectory` returns success without locking again. The lock is released when the `BlockManager` is destroyed rather than at exit. That happens at shutdown, and when a GUI user retries a failed chainstate load with a reindex, after which the new `BlockManager` reacquires it. A blocks directory used through the kernel now has to be writable, as bitcoind already required.

Added a regression test to feature_filelock.py.
</description>

diff --git a/src/node/blockstorage.h b/src/node/blockstorage.h
index c4cc34cb2e..4b90b4534f 100644
--- a/src/node/blockstorage.h
+++ b/src/node/blockstorage.h
@@ -183,6 +183,22 @@ enum class ReadRawError {
     BadPartRange,
 };
 
+/**
+ * Instances for the same directory in one process share one lock, and
+ * destroying any of them releases it.
+ */
+class BlocksDirLock
+{
+    const fs::path m_dir;
+
+public:
+    explicit BlocksDirLock(fs::path dir);
+    ~BlocksDirLock();
+
+    BlocksDirLock(const BlocksDirLock&) = delete;
+    BlocksDirLock& operator=(const BlocksDirLock&) = delete;
+};
+
 /**
  * Maintains a tree of blocks (stored in `m_block_index`) which is consulted
  * to determine where the most-work tip is.
@@ -196,6 +212,10 @@ class BlockManager
     friend ChainstateManager;
 
 private:
+    //! First member, so the lock is held before any other member uses the
+    //! blocks directory and until all of them are destroyed.
+    const BlocksDirLock m_blocks_dir_lock;
+
     const CChainParams& GetParams() const { return m_opts.chainparams; }
     const Consensus::Params& GetConsensus() const { return m_opts.chainparams.GetConsensus(); }
     /**
diff --git a/src/node/blockstorage.cpp b/src/node/blockstorage.cpp
index b8c31dbd2e..544c71a1c5 100644
--- a/src/node/blockstorage.cpp
+++ b/src/node/blockstorage.cpp
@@ -30,6 +30,7 @@
 #include <util/check.h>
 #include <util/expected.h>
 #include <util/fs.h>
+#include <util/fs_helpers.h>
 #include <util/log.h>
 #include <util/obfuscation.h>
 #include <util/overflow.h>
@@ -1179,6 +1180,24 @@ FlatFilePos BlockManager::WriteBlock(const CBlock& block, int nHeight)
     return pos;
 }
 
+BlocksDirLock::BlocksDirLock(fs::path dir) : m_dir{std::move(dir)}
+{
+    switch (util::LockDirectory(m_dir, ".lock")) {
+    case util::LockResult::ErrorWrite:
+        throw std::runtime_error{strprintf("Cannot write to directory '%s'; check permissions.", fs::PathToString(m_dir))};
+    case util::LockResult::ErrorLock:
+        throw std::runtime_error{strprintf("Cannot obtain a lock on directory %s. It is probably in use by another process.", fs::PathToString(m_dir))};
+    case util::LockResult::Success:
+        return;
+    }
+    assert(false);
+}
+
+BlocksDirLock::~BlocksDirLock()
+{
+    UnlockDirectory(m_dir, ".lock");
+}
+
 static auto InitBlocksdirXorKey(const BlockManager::Options& opts)
 {
     // Bytes are serialized without length indicator, so this is also the exact
@@ -1231,7 +1250,8 @@ static auto InitBlocksdirXorKey(const BlockManager::Options& opts)
 }
 
 BlockManager::BlockManager(const util::SignalInterrupt& interrupt, Options opts)
-    : m_prune_mode{opts.prune_target > 0},
+    : m_blocks_dir_lock{opts.blocks_dir},
+      m_prune_mode{opts.prune_target > 0},
       m_obfuscation{InitBlocksdirXorKey(opts)},
       m_opts{std::move(opts)},
       m_block_file_seq{FlatFileSeq{m_opts.blocks_dir, "blk", m_opts.fast_prune ? 0x4000 /* 16kB */ : BLOCKFILE_CHUNK_SIZE}},
diff --git a/test/functional/feature_filelock.py b/test/functional/feature_filelock.py
index 0887cac263..c827302f58 100755
--- a/test/functional/feature_filelock.py
+++ b/test/functional/feature_filelock.py
@@ -2,15 +2,18 @@
 # Copyright (c) 2018-present The Bitcoin Core developers
 # Distributed under the MIT software license, see the accompanying
 # file COPYING or http://www.opensource.org/licenses/mit-license.php.
-"""Check that it's not possible to start a second bitcoind instance using the same datadir or wallet."""
+"""Check that it's not possible to start a second bitcoind instance using the same datadir or wallet,
+or to run bitcoin-chainstate on the blocksdir of a running bitcoind."""
 import random
 import string
+import subprocess
 
 from test_framework.test_framework import BitcoinTestFramework
 from test_framework.test_node import (
     BITCOIN_PID_FILENAME_DEFAULT,
     ErrorMatch,
 )
+from test_framework.util import assert_equal
 
 class FilelockTest(BitcoinTestFramework):
     def set_test_params(self):
@@ -51,5 +54,23 @@ class FilelockTest(BitcoinTestFramework):
             expected_msg = f"Error: SQLiteDatabase: Unable to obtain an exclusive lock on the database, is it being used by another instance of {self.config['environment']['CLIENT_NAME']}?"
             self.nodes[1].assert_start_raises_init_error(extra_args=[f'-walletdir={wallet_dir}', f'-wallet={wallet_name}', '-noserver'], expected_msg=expected_msg, match=ErrorMatch.PARTIAL_REGEX)
 
+        if self.is_bitcoin_chainstate_compiled():
+            self.log.info("Check that bitcoin-chainstate can't use the blocksdir of a running bitcoind")
+            blocksdir_root = self.nodes[1].datadir_path / "blocksdir"
+            blocksdir_root.mkdir()
+            self.start_node(1, extra_args=[f"-blocksdir={blocksdir_root}"])
+            # bitcoin-chainstate uses <datadir>/blocks as its blocksdir, so this
+            # gives it node1's block files with an empty block index of its own.
+            chainstate_datadir = blocksdir_root / self.chain
+            result = subprocess.run(
+                self.get_binaries().chainstate_argv() + ["-regtest", chainstate_datadir],
+                input="",
+                capture_output=True,
+                text=True,
+                timeout=5 * self.options.timeout_factor,
+            )
+            assert_equal(result.returncode, 1)
+            assert f"Cannot obtain a lock on directory {chainstate_datadir / 'blocks'}." in result.stdout
+
 if __name__ == '__main__':
     FilelockTest(__file__).main()
